page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyperthreading. The configuration provides 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor integrates advanced instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 matrix engines, SHA-NI, and VAES. It features 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache.

The instance does not include bundled local instance storage, requiring remote Premium Storage for persistent file systems and OS disks. It also lacks hardware GPU accelerators and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic testing reflects the throughput boundaries of a single physical execution core, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the average band at 1942.19, while multi-core scoring reaches 1991.97. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 21.51 GB/sec for reads and 14.04 GB/sec for writes. PassMark database operations register at 1604.83, and Redis SET throughput yields 2.56 million operations per second.

Hardware capabilities such as AMX provide baseline acceleration for low-intensity inference, reaching 91.22 tokens per second on small 135M language models. However, parallel workloads such as Clang compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving are constrained by the dual-thread ceiling of the underlying single core. The E2s_v6 provides a memory-dense footprint suited for small in-memory caches, lightweight relational databases, intermediate microservices, and memory-sensitive enterprise tasks requiring substantial memory per execution thread without broad parallel compute demands.
description: Microsoft Azure E2s_v6 is an entry-level memory-optimized instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, backed by a single hyperthreaded physical core of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Designed with an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, it incorporates modern vector and matrix extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance lacks bundled local storage, requiring network-attached Premium Storage disks for data persistence, and operates without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-thread execution, reaching a Geekbench single-core score of 1648.0 and handling small-scale model text generation at 91.22 tokens per second, although aggregate multi-core throughput and uncached memory bandwidth remain constrained by the single-core topology. The instance is suited for low-concurrency in-memory data stores, lightweight relational databases, and enterprise background services requiring dedicated per-thread memory allocation.
